title: AI Security Threat Triage for Business Proposals (2026)

questions.question: What is the composite verdict when any category contains a HIGH signal?
options: PROCEED, because a single high signal can be isolated in implementation
PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, because the security milestone handles high signals
HARD STOP, with security-architect sign-off conditions for each HIGH category
The engine averages HIGH with the other three category scores
questions.explanation: compute_verdict checks high_hits first. Any HIGH severity returns HARD_STOP and creates a security-architect sign-off condition for the matching category.

questions.question: How does triage classify the internal analytics dashboard that uses an internal API but no uploads or external tools?
options: HARD STOP, because every API is an external tool
PROCEED, because internal data has no security category
HARD STOP, because a LOW signal counts as two MEDIUM signals
PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, because the API is one MEDIUM external-tool signal
questions.explanation: The description matches 'internal' as LOW sensitive data and 'api' as one MEDIUM external-tools signal. With exactly one medium and no high, compute_verdict returns PROCEED_WITH_CONDITIONS.

questions.question: Why does the document assistant proposal receive HARD STOP?
options: The 'upload' signal is HIGH prompt-injection risk; that single HIGH hit is enough for HARD STOP
The word employee creates a HIGH identity signal even without impersonation
The MEDIUM employee/contract matches alone trigger HARD STOP, even without the upload signal
A SharePoint destination automatically makes every data category CRITICAL
questions.explanation: The text matches employee and contract as MEDIUM sensitive-data signals, while 'upload' is a HIGH prompt-injection signal. That single HIGH category is enough for HARD_STOP; the MEDIUM hits are additional context, not the trigger.

questions.question: What makes the CRM agent proposal a HARD STOP rather than a conditional review?
options: Only the customer-data signal is MEDIUM, so it should proceed with one condition
High external-tool and identity signals appear: it updates CRM, sends mail, and acts on behalf of a user
The internal Salesforce data is automatically outside every security scope
The engine cannot parse a sentence containing more than one action
questions.explanation: The description matches updates crm/send email as HIGH external-tool signals and on behalf of as HIGH identity ambiguity. Those HIGH hits trigger HARD_STOP before medium counts are considered.

questions.question: What verdict does compute_verdict return for exactly one MEDIUM category and no HIGH categories?
options: PROCEED, because one medium signal is below the hard-stop count
HARD STOP, because every medium signal requires an architect veto
PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, including a security milestone and an ADR entry
HARD STOP, because the category list must contain four LOW results
questions.explanation: The one-medium branch returns PROCEED_WITH_CONDITIONS. It asks for a security-review milestone before MVP and records the matched signal in the architecture decision record.

questions.question: What happens when a description contains customer data and an API call but no HIGH signal?
options: PROCEED, because customer data is only MEDIUM and APIs are not scored
HARD STOP, because two MEDIUM categories are treated as a combined HIGH
PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, because the two signals are merged into one review item
HARD STOP, because two MEDIUM categories cross the composite stop rule
questions.explanation: customer data produces MEDIUM sensitive-data exposure and api produces MEDIUM external-tool access. With two medium results, compute_verdict returns HARD_STOP even without a HIGH signal.
